## Concept

### Pitch

The [SidebarScope](../sidebar/index.md#sidebar-scope) along the left of the main window, beside the [BodyScope](../../../scope/application/Body.md#body-scope), holding the tools for finding your way around the project.

### Shape

#### Description

Runs the full height of the window beneath the ribbon, to the left of the body, and the chat input along its bottom. The file tree fills it from the top, and the git panel sits along the bottom, underneath it, taking only the height it needs, up to half the sidebar, or up to where the edge between them has been dragged, as the [GitPanelScope](../git-panel/index.md#git-panel-scope) says.

#### Others

It is the only sidebar on the body's left. While a task runs, a second one, the running task's referenced spec, slides out at the right of the message list and the chat input, as the [RightSidebarScope](../right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar-scope) says.

A ProjectSidebarScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A ProjectSidebarScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable beh

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Side

left

## Width

260

## Min Width

160

## Panels

- [FileTreeScope](../file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope)
- [GitPanelScope](../git-panel/index.md#git-panel-scope)

## Sidebar

It runs along the left of what it sits beside, with a thin line down its right edge, where the two meet. It is resized by dragging that edge: it starts 260 pixels wide and can't be dragged narrower than 160.

        between one panel and the next, where the lower panel's header meets
        the body of the one above, is a handle: dragging it up or down moves

content.text:
I replaced the old left sidebar with a new **LeftSidebar** that has a VS Code / JetBrains-style strip of view icons down its left edge, and moved the Run panels into it. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 82 files.

- **New LeftSidebar** (`.claude/reference/ui/components/left-sidebar/index.md`):
  - **View bar** (`#view-bar`): a 40px icon strip on the darkest surface with three views.
    - **Files** (Ctrl+Shift+E).
    - **Git** (Ctrl+Shift+G), with a badge counting uncommitted files.
    - **Run** (Ctrl+Shift+R), with a spinner while a task runs and a dot when one has started since you last looked.
  - **Selected view:** shown with an accent bar and full-strength icon.
  - **Collapsing:** clicking the view already showing collapses the sidebar to just the bar.
  - **Views** (`#views`, `#run-view`):
    - Files and Git each get the full height. The draggable edge between the file tree and Git is gone.
    - Run holds the referenced files, understanding and subagents panels, sized and resizable as before.
    - With no task yet, Run says "No task running". After a task ends, Run keeps showing it until the next one starts.
  - **No automatic switching** (`#following`): Files shows to start with, and the sidebar never switches to Run by itself.
- **Right sidebar:** now holds only the Tasks list, with no tab row. It still shows while a task runs or is queued, or when you open it.
- **Removed:** the old Project Sidebar spec is gone. The Git panel and the three Run panels now point to their new homes.

**Choices to check:**
- The keyboard shortcuts are mine.
- Ctrl+Shift+R may clash with something on your setup.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `LeftSidebarScope` `#description`, `#view-bar`, `#views`, `#following` and `#run-view`; `RightSidebarScope` `#description` and `#showing`; `GitPanelScope`; `TasksTabScope` `#virtualized`; and `BodyScope` and `MainWindowScope` for where the sidebars sit.
